subject: Logic
title: The Violinist
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Violinist.

hook.text: You wake up connected to a famous violinist. Unplug and he dies. Must you stay connected for nine months?

buildup.text: Judith Jarvis Thomson designed this in 1971 to explore bodily autonomy even when another life is at stake.

discovery.text: Most people say unplugging is permissible—you didn't choose this connection and your body is your own.

twist.text: Thomson argues this holds even if the violinist has full rights. Rights don't include using someone else's body.

climax.text: The experiment separates the right to life from the right to use another person's body to sustain it.

punchline.text: Having a right to life ≠ having a right to someone else's body.

quiz.question: What principle does the Violinist thought experiment explore?
options: Bodily autonomy versus the right to life
